items.simple_meaning: A doctor is a person who helps sick people get well.
items.explanation: When you feel unwell, a doctor checks you and tells you how to feel better. Doctors work in clinics and hospitals.
items.example_sentence: The doctor checked my throat when I had a cold in the monsoon.
items.real_world_usage: Mummy, I want to be a doctor when I grow up!
items.learning_objective: Children will name a doctor and say how a doctor helps people.
items.illustration_brief: A friendly doctor with a stethoscope gently listening to a smiling child's heartbeat in a bright, cheerful clinic.

items.simple_meaning: A driver is a person who makes a car, bus or other vehicle move and go places.
items.explanation: A driver sits at the steering wheel and takes people where they need to go. The school bus driver takes children to school safely.
items.example_sentence: Our school bus driver waves to us every morning.
items.real_world_usage: Thank you, driver uncle, for taking us to school!
items.learning_objective: Children will name a driver and understand that a driver controls a vehicle.
items.illustration_brief: A smiling driver at the wheel of a yellow school bus, with happy children sitting in their seats behind.

items.simple_meaning: The neck is the part of the body that joins your head to your shoulders.
items.explanation: Your neck helps you turn your head to look left and right. You can wear a scarf around your neck in winter.
items.example_sentence: Dadi wrapped a warm scarf around my neck on the cold winter morning.
items.real_world_usage: Look, I can turn my neck to see the birds!
items.spelling_guidance: Neck ends with 'ck', like duck and rock.
items.learning_objective: Children will point to and name their neck as a body part.
items.illustration_brief: A child gently touching their neck with a cosy scarf around it, alongside a giraffe stretching its long neck.

items.simple_meaning: A market is a place where people buy and sell things.
items.explanation: At a market, there are many shops or stalls selling fruits, vegetables, clothes and more. People go there to buy what they need.
items.example_sentence: We went to the market to buy flowers and sweets for Diwali.
items.real_world_usage: Can I come with you to the market, Papa?
items.spelling_guidance: Break it into two parts: mar + ket.
items.learning_objective: Children will name a market as a place to buy and sell things.
items.illustration_brief: A busy, colourful market with stalls of fruits, vegetables and flowers, and a family carrying a cloth shopping bag.

items.simple_meaning: A farm is land where people grow crops or keep animals.
items.explanation: Farmers grow rice, wheat and vegetables on a farm. Some farms also have cows, goats and hens.
items.example_sentence: During the holidays, we saw cows and green rice fields at Nana's farm.
items.real_world_usage: I saw a hen and her chicks at the farm!
items.spelling_guidance: Farm has the sound 'ar' like in car: f-a-r-m.
items.learning_objective: Children will describe a farm as a place with crops and animals.
items.illustration_brief: A sunny farm with green fields, a cow, a goat, hens and a small farmhouse under a blue sky.

items.simple_meaning: A mountain is very high land that rises far above the ground around it.
items.explanation: Mountains are much taller than hills. Some mountains have snow on top.
items.example_sentence: On our holiday, we saw a tall mountain with white snow on top.
items.real_world_usage: Look, that mountain is touching the clouds!
items.spelling_guidance: Split it: moun + tain. Remember 'ai' in the second part.
items.learning_objective: Children will recognise and name a mountain as very high land.
items.illustration_brief: Tall green and grey mountains with snowy peaks, a river flowing in the valley and soft clouds around the tops.

items.simple_meaning: A bottle is a container used to hold water, milk or other drinks.
items.explanation: A bottle has a narrow top and a lid. You carry a water bottle to school to drink when you are thirsty.
items.example_sentence: I fill my water bottle before I go to school.
items.real_world_usage: Mumma, please put my bottle in my school bag.
items.spelling_guidance: Bottle has double 't' and ends with 'le': b-o-t-t-l-e.
items.learning_objective: Children will name a bottle and say what it holds.
items.illustration_brief: A colourful water bottle with a lid standing next to a school bag and a tiffin box.

items.simple_meaning: A shower is a place in the bathroom where water sprays down to wash your body.
items.explanation: When you turn on the shower, water comes down from above like rain. You can take a shower to get clean.
items.example_sentence: After playing cricket in the park, I took a shower at home.
items.real_world_usage: I want to take a shower now, I am all sweaty!
items.spelling_guidance: Shower has 'ow' like in cow, then 'er': sh-ow-er.
items.learning_objective: Children will name a shower and link it to keeping clean.
items.illustration_brief: A clean bathroom with water gently spraying from a shower head, with soap, a bucket and a fluffy towel nearby.

items.simple_meaning: A daughter is a girl child of a mother and father.
items.explanation: If a family has a girl child, she is their daughter. A girl is always her parents' daughter, even when she grows up.
items.example_sentence: Meera is the daughter of Aunty Priya and Uncle Raj.
items.real_world_usage: I am Mummy and Papa's daughter.
items.learning_objective: Children will understand that a daughter is a girl child in a family.
items.illustration_brief: A happy family of a mother, a father and their young daughter holding hands together in a garden.

items.simple_meaning: A seat is a place where you can sit.
items.explanation: Chairs, benches and sofas all have seats. In a bus or car, you sit on a seat.
items.example_sentence: Please sit on your seat while Teacher reads the story.
items.real_world_usage: Dadi, you can have my seat.
items.spelling_guidance: Seat has 'ea' that says the long 'ee' sound.
items.learning_objective: Children will name a seat and use it in a polite sentence.
items.illustration_brief: A cosy living room with a chair and a sofa, and a child kindly offering a seat to a grandparent.
